title: Epochal telemetry-driven slotted scheduler for multi-GPU prefill/decode
creator: Aisha Park
description: Design and implement a telemetry-aware slotted scheduling layer (Epochal Scheduler) that coordinates tensor/pipeline parallel handoffs and NCCL windows to maximize NCCL overlap while preserving latency SLOs for single-request decode. The scheduler should use lightweight per-epoch telemetry (device utilization, token latencies, KV cache hit patterns) to pick kernel hints, create micro-windows for all-reduce/collective overlap, and time prefill handoffs to reduce blocking stalls across heterogeneous GPUs.
motivation: We observe intermittent tail latency spikes when running mixed prefill and decode workloads on heterogeneous multi-GPU nodes. Current heuristics pick kernels and handoff points without using live telemetry, leading to suboptimal NCCL overlap and stalls during prefill->decode transitions. This ticket targets a coordinated solution that learns short-term device states and pre-schedules comm windows to hide communication latency under computation.
acceptance_criteria: Scheduler integrates with runtime telemetry API and emits epoch decisions every 50-200ms
Prefill->decode end-to-end p99 latency reduced by >= 20% on our heterogeneous 8xA10 cluster for mixed workloads
NCCL all-reduce idle time decreased by >= 30% measured via per-epoch comm-util metrics
No regressions on steady-state throughput (<5% variance) for batched requests
A/B rollout hooks exist in console and feature flag guarded; can be disabled at route level
design_notes: Epochs: use 100ms default epoch length with adaptive expansion under heavy congestion
Telemetry signals: device_gpu_util, ring_bw_estimate, kv_cache_hit_rate, recent_kernel_latencies, inflight_prefill_count
Slots: subdivide epoch into 3 slot types - compute-priority, comm-window, hybrid-window. Assign slots per microbatch wave.
Kernel hinting: runtime exposes soft-hints (quantized kernels, fused-attn variants). Scheduler appends kernel_hint metadata to microbatches to bias kernel selection
Fallback: when telemetry unavailable, fall back to conservative kernel set and shorter comm windows to favor latency
Heterogeneity handling: per-device epoch weights to bias slot assignments to faster devices; use stride-aware token sharding to align comm bursts
tradeoffs: Epoch duration vs reactivity: shorter epochs adapt faster but add scheduling overhead; we pick 100ms as default and make it tunable per node
Aggressive NCCL overlap increases compute jitter risk - may hurt single-request tail if not constrained by SLO knobs
Telemetry sampling adds low CPU/PCIe overhead; we limit signal set to 6 metrics to avoid measurement noise
Complexity: introduces centralized epoch coordinator within a node conductor — simplifies cross-stage decisions at cost of more orchestration code
implementation_plan: Phase 1 (spike, 1 week): prototype epoch coordinator that reads telemetry and emits slot schedule; unit test offline traces
Phase 2 (2 weeks): integrate kernel_hint plumbing into runtime microbatch descriptor; add slot enforcement in prefill/decode orchestrator
Phase 3 (2 weeks): implement NCCL window priming hooks and per-device slot assignments; add metrics export
Phase 4 (1 week): run GPU-cluster experiments, tune epoch length and slot ratios; gather p99/p95 metrics
Phase 5 (1 week): console feature flag, rollout plan, and PR/QA
test_plan: Unit tests for epoch decision logic and kernel_hint mapping
Integration tests using synthetic mixed prefill/decode traces in our sim harness
Performance tests on 4xA10 and 8xA100 hetero nodes for standard workloads and adversarial token length patterns
Chaos tests: force telemetry gaps and verify fallback path
Regression: run nightly perf job to validate throughput and latency invariants
rollout_plan: Start with canary on internal 'dev' cluster (10% of requests) behind feature flag
Collect per-route latency and NCCL util metrics for 48 hours
Ramp to 50% with automatic rollback if p99 increases by >5% or comm idle not decreasing
Full rollout to dedicated nodes after 1 week of stable metrics
Expose route-level knob in Console to disable scheduler per-customer
progress_updates: 2026-02-16: Spike started. Built a minimal epoch coordinator in Python to replay traces from perf-harness. Observed patterns where comm windows could be aligned to overlapping prefill waves.
2026-02-20: Kernel hint API proposal shared with runtime team. Feedback: keep hints idempotent and low-cardinality to avoid combinatorial kernel selection explosion.
2026-02-24: Prototype integrated into conductor; initial synthetic tests show 15% reduction in NCCL idle for synchronous prefill-heavy traces.
2026-03-01: Began implementing kernel_hint in C++ runtime path and added telemetry sampling stub. Assigned infra ticket for extended metrics storage.
review_feedback: PM (Nora Patel): Ensure we have clear safety limits — don't worsen single-request latency for small requests.
Design (Liam Chen): Prefer heuristics expressed as tunable lamdas rather than hard thresholds to make experiments easier.
Runtime (Elena Gomez): Avoid cross-thread locking in epoch coordinator hot path; use lock-free snapshots of telemetry rings.
SRE (Oliver Kim): Add observability for slot assignment heatmaps and NCCL overlap ratios before rolling to prod
incident_learnings: From INC-2025-11: uncoordinated prefill on heterogeneous devices caused 2x p99 regressions. Root cause: simultaneous all-reduce waves blocked on slower device
We must ensure graceful degradation: scheduler should detect persistent slow devices and reduce their slot allocation
